sections.html:
Owners in Peachtree Corners usually weigh a broker listing, a private sale and an as-is cash purchase, and house age and condition drive the decision. The 2025 estimate shows 42,519 residents, barely above the 42,259 in the 2020 base. That 0.6% change points to a built-out city where most sales involve houses and townhomes that already exist.

Of 17,799 households, 53.0% live in homes they own. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $484,700, and typical rent is $1,701. Land area is 16.11 square miles and density is 2,623 people per square mile, so condos, townhomes and single-family houses sit close together. Price your house from sales inside your own subdivision, because a citywide figure blends all of them.

Voters approved incorporation on November 8, 2011, and the city began operating on July 1, 2012 as Gwinnett's 16th and largest. About 17 square miles in Gwinnett's southwest corner belong to the city, and seven miles of the Chattahoochee River mark its western edge. Interstate 85, Interstate 285 and Georgia 400 are all nearby.

Landmarks help a buyer place your house: Curiosity Lab, a city-owned testing ground with a 3-mile autonomous vehicle track inside a 500-acre technology park; Town Center, a 21-acre development at 5200 Town Center Boulevard with shops, restaurants and a Town Green; and river parks with trout fishing, kayaking and boating. Gwinnett County Public Schools serve the city, including a STEM school, alongside private and parochial options.

The city says its millage rate is zero and it charges no property tax of its own. Gwinnett County bills the parcel, and owners get one combined bill with city and county items. Service fees can still appear on it, so read every line before you tell a buyer what the house costs to carry.

One fee is specific to the city. Peachtree Corners replaced neighborhood-by-neighborhood streetlight assessments with two citywide rates, $60 a year for residential properties and $180 for commercial ones, and an owner is not charged both the old and new amounts. Streets that adopted speed humps also carry a small annual assessment in that district, which shows up on the tax bill. Have your closing attorney check whether either charge applies to your parcel, and keep the paid receipts with your sale papers.

For appeals, Gwinnett gives 45 days from the date on the annual notice, and residential questions go to the Assessors at 770-822-7200. Business inventory, boats and aircraft are handled separately at 770-822-7220.

sections.h2: Streetlight fee and speed hump assessments
sections.html:
The citywide streetlight fee exempts federal, state and county properties and HOA-owned parcels, because the homes inside an HOA already pay the residential rate. Vacant residential and commercial parcels do pay, since they benefit from the same lit roads.

Speed humps work differently. After a traffic study, a street's owners vote by petition, the city pays for installation, and each platted lot in that service area carries an annual maintenance assessment on its tax bill, built or not. If your street has humps, mention the assessment to buyers up front.

City Hall, Gwinnett County and the state each own a piece of the services around a home, so it helps to know whom to ring.

Gwinnett County supplies police and fire protection under agreements with the city. State routes, including Buford Highway, Jimmy Carter Boulevard and Peachtree Parkway, answer to the Georgia Department of Transportation.

Peachtree Corners enforces a property maintenance code on owners and landlords alike. Exterior items the city lists include:

  • Weeds above 12 inches
  • Inoperable or unlicensed vehicles
  • Pools and spas left dirty
  • Damaged fences and walls
  • Accumulated trash

Rentals must meet interior standards covering plumbing, heat, handrails, light and ventilation, and the owner must fix leaks, electrical hazards and broken windows.

Trees need special care. A homeowner may remove a tree without a permit unless it stands in a required zoning buffer, conservation area, open space, the Chattahoochee River Corridor or a designated tree save area, or qualifies as a specimen tree. The city defines a specimen as a hardwood of 28 inches or more, a softwood of 30 inches or more, or a native flowering tree of 12 inches or more, measured 4.5 feet above ground. A lot within 2,000 linear feet of the river is in the corridor, and owners must keep at least two live trees. There is no permit fee, although mitigation costs may apply to a landmark or specimen tree.

sections.h2: Who owes the bill when a house sells mid-year?
sections.html: Gwinnett ties liability to the January 1 owner, and a mid-year sale produces a bill for each side. Ask the closing attorney to write the contract so the buyer expressly accepts the tax, using language like "Seller assigns the liability for the payment of property taxes to the purchaser and purchaser accepts such assignment." The commissioner rejects vague text such as "Unpaid taxes not accounted for in the closing statement are the responsibility of the seller and buyer to prorate." Taxes paid on time need no extra paperwork. If the bill goes unpaid, the January 1 owner stays on any lien unless assumption proof, the new deed and its recording are done within 90 days of the due date.

The Georgia Department of Revenue treats the real estate transfer tax as the seller's cost unless the contract says otherwise, and it must be paid before the deed is recorded. Ask the Gwinnett clerk of superior court for current recording fees, and have your attorney e-file the PT-61.

A well-kept house usually earns the most through a broker listing. A private sale works for owners ready to price and negotiate alone, and a cash purchase skips repairs and showings, which helps with an inherited house, a tenant in place or a firm deadline. Gather the deed, a recent tax bill, permits and any HOA documents first, then compare written offers by what you net. Ask each buyer when funds arrive and whether the offer depends on a loan, an inspection or repairs.

faqs.q: Does the city of Peachtree Corners tax my house?
faqs.a: The city states a zero millage rate. Gwinnett bills the parcel, and the bill may list service fees such as the $60 residential streetlight fee. Call the Tax Commissioner at 770-822-8800 for the lines on your account.

faqs.q: Who handles tree questions on a Peachtree Corners lot?
faqs.a: Public Works at City Hall, 678-691-1200. Permits are required for trees in buffers, conservation areas, tree save areas, the river corridor and for specimen trees, and each lot must keep at least two live trees.

faqs.q: What if I sell partway through the year?
faqs.a: Gwinnett bills both sides. The January 1 owner stays on any lien unless assumption proof, the new deed and its recording are done within 90 days of the due date.

faqs.q: What is the Gwinnett appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date printed on the annual Notice of Assessment. Real property questions go to the Assessors at 770-822-7200.

faqs.q: Who answers emergency calls in Peachtree Corners?
faqs.a: Gwinnett County police and fire serve the city under intergovernmental agreements. Dial 911 in an emergency and 770-513-5700 for non-emergency police matters.
